blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At portfolio level, cross-docking and flow strategies are less about individual warehouses and more about the overall tempo of the operation. A company that routes 50% of its volume through cross-dock moves its cost base, its working capital and its risk profile all at the same time. The decision is not operational; it is strategic, and it deserves board-level attention because the trade-offs are real.

Cross-docking reduces storage cost and working capital, but only works where demand is steady and suppliers are reliable. Classic distribution absorbs variability and protects service, but at the cost of inventory and space. The question at senior level is not whether one model is better, but which mix fits the business as it actually operates — and whether the mix in place reflects a conscious decision or an accumulation of old ones.

Had we reviewed the mix seriously three years ago, we would have freed meaningful capital and moved faster on two new segments. That review was not glamorous work. Almost all important strategic logistics work is not.

items.q: According to the text, why does the cross-docking decision deserve board-level attention?
options: Because it always improves service levels
Because it moves cost base, working capital and risk profile at once
Because it is a purely operational matter
items.why: "moves its cost base, its working capital and its risk profile all at the same time… it is strategic."

items.q: What does classic distribution offer that cross-docking does not?
options: The ability to absorb variability and protect service
items.why: "Classic distribution absorbs variability and protects service, but at the cost of inventory and space."

items.q: According to the text, the real question at senior level is…
options: which mix fits the business as it actually operates
which supplier offers the lowest price
which single model is objectively better
items.why: "not whether one model is better, but which mix fits the business as it actually operates."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: The flow model reshapes the company's risk profile.
Cross-docking is glamorous work that attracts easy attention.
The current mix may simply be an accumulation of past choices.
Cross-docking depends on steady demand and reliable suppliers.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que esse trabalho "was not glamorous" — o autor discordaria de que seja glamoroso.

items.q: The final sentence — "Almost all important strategic logistics work is not [glamorous]" — suggests that…
options: logistics should be handed to junior staff
value in logistics often comes from unglamorous, disciplined work
only visible projects create real value
items.why: Inferência: o autor valoriza o trabalho difícil e pouco vistoso justamente por ser o que gera resultado estratégico.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver apresentando a revisão de portfólio ao comitê. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thank you. Let me be direct about where this review has landed, because the number surprised even me. We came in assuming we would keep roughly thirty per cent of volume on cross-dock. The evidence points somewhere quite different — closer to fifty-five per cent.

Two thirds of what we currently hold in regional distribution centres serves segments where demand is steady and our suppliers are, frankly, dependable. That inventory is not protecting service. It is sitting there, tying up working capital and hiding the fact that the flow is already reliable enough to cross-dock.

Now, I want to be careful. There are two segments — the project business and the spare-parts line — where variability is genuine, and I am not touching those. Classic distribution earns its keep there. But for the rest, the case is clear.

If we move to fifty-five per cent, we free roughly eight million in working capital, and that is what lets us fund entry into the two new segments without going back to the board for more cash. Had we done this three years ago, we would already be operating in both. So my recommendation is that we sign off on the shift now and roll it out region by region over the next two quarters.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What share of volume does Oliver now recommend for cross-docking?
items.why: "The evidence points somewhere quite different — closer to fifty-five per cent."

items.q: Why does Oliver say the inventory in regional centres is a problem?
options: It ties up working capital and hides that the flow is already reliable
It is spread across too many sites
items.why: "tying up working capital and hiding the fact that the flow is already reliable enough to cross-dock."

items.q: Which segments will Oliver deliberately keep on classic distribution?
options: The two new segments he wants to enter
The project business and the spare-parts line
items.why: "two segments — the project business and the spare-parts line — where variability is genuine, and I am not touching those."

items.q: What can be inferred about the ~£8 million in freed working capital?
options: It will be returned to shareholders
It will be spent on new warehouses
It funds entry into two new segments without asking the board for more cash
It covers a shortfall in the current budget
items.why: Inferência: ele diz que o capital liberado é "what lets us fund entry into the two new segments without going back to the board for more cash."

items.q: What does Oliver imply with "Had we done this three years ago, we would already be operating in both"?
options: The review was completed too early
The delay has already cost the company opportunity
The board rejected the idea before
The two segments are no longer worth entering
items.why: Inferência (conditional perfect): a inação passada custou tempo de mercado — eles já estariam nos dois segmentos.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Cross-docking changes the overall tempo of the operation." Here, tempo means…
options: the rhythm or pace at which things move
items.why: Tempo = ritmo, cadência com que a operação se move.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Routing volume through cross-dock lowers our ___, because we hold far less stock at any moment."
items.why: Working capital = capital de giro; menos estoque parado libera capital de giro.

items.q: "Classic distribution exists to absorb variability." To absorb variability means to…
options: pass the swings on to suppliers
cushion or take up swings so service is protected
items.why: To absorb = absorver: o estoque amortece as oscilações de demanda.

items.q: Risk profile is best described as…
options: the overall shape and level of risk the business carries
items.why: Risk profile = perfil de risco: o conjunto e a intensidade dos riscos que a operação assume.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The current mix is not a decision; it is an ___ of choices no one has revisited."
items.why: Accumulation = acumulação: o mix atual é um acúmulo de decisões antigas nunca revisadas.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem numa revisão de portfólio logístico. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The committee still has to sign off on the shift to 55%." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the new model region by region." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, por etapas.

items.q: "That inventory is tying up eight million in capital." To tie up capital means to…
options: lock it away so it cannot be used elsewhere
items.why: Tie up capital = imobilizar capital, deixá-lo preso e indisponível.

items.q: "Two operations managers pushed back on the spare-parts exception." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "Freeing that working capital is what genuinely moves the needle on growth." This means it…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, causar um impacto perceptível.
